ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in the figure, point C is a point on line segment AB, M and N are the midpoints of AB and CB respectively, with $AC=10\,cm$ and $NB=6\,cm$. Find the length of MN.
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is a horizontal line segment, with the points labeled from left to right as A, C, M, N, B, therefore C is on AB, and the image order shows M to the left of N and N to the right of M. Reasoning: According to the specified coordinate method, let A=0. It is known that AC=10 cm, so C=10. Let B=b. Because M is the midpoint of AB, the coordinate of M is b/2. Because N is the midpoint of CB, the coordinate of N is (10+b)/2. Thus the length of MN is N-M=(10+b)/2-b/2=10/2=5 cm. In the figure N is to the right of M, so this difference is exactly the length of line segment MN.
